lessons.text: Prepare an answer before you assert: Thomas Edison broke through with "However, your premise assumes what it needs to prove, and the data shows otherwise. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the pre…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Prepare an answer before you assert: Thomas Edison broke through with "But note what just happened: your argument skipped the evidence entirely. Because car bans make downtowns worse, the documented cases show…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Borrow this pattern from Thomas Edison: "Yet your position leaves the strongest counter-example untouched. When the measured results are compared across studies, then the pattern i…" — it answered the opponent directly, its premises led cleanly to the conclusion.
Your weakest move against Thomas Edison was "It is obvious that car-free downtowns make cities better." (soundness 0.65). State its premises and evidence before you use it again.
